summary.text: A 37-year-old man with no significant past medical history presented to the emergency department with palpitations. His electrocardiogram showed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at 129 beats per minute, while the blood count, metabolic panel, troponin and echocardiogram were unremarkable or negative. He appeared well and was hemodynamically stable.

He received intravenous diltiazem 30 mg over four hours in the emergency department but remained in atrial fibrillation with a heart rate in the 80s. A remote virtual hospital team took over his care, he was given aspirin and 150 mg of oral diltiazem before leaving, and was placed on a cellular 12-lead telemetry device at home, rather than being admitted.

At home he had 49 episodes of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, all rate controlled with oral diltiazem under remote cardiologist direction, and emergency response was never initiated. He spontaneously converted to sinus rhythm the next morning, had a video cardiology consult with stress test and repeat echo ordered, and was discharged from remote monitoring; sinus rhythm was maintained at seven days.
